representedDate: Standing museum after the 2012 redevelopment and 2020 depot reroofing
wholePhysicalScope: The connected Toitū Otago Settlers Museum in Dunedin, with the Edwardian Burnside galleries, rounded Art Deco rail depot, rear collections ranges and modern glazed Josephine Foyer.
lodDetails: All four levels preserve the pointed glass foyer, Edwardian brick galleries and long Art Deco range with its red sawtooth roof. Near tiers add arch moldings, transoms and pilaster bays.
limitations: Joined exterior; component joins and precise height distribution are approximate. The original Burnside façade uses its dated postcard, and the modern entry uses the Qualla CC0 foyer image and written design account.

The three main faces, corner curvature, depot saw-toothed roof and glazing capture the published architectural distinctions. Recent signage, art, fixtures and display interiors are outside the model scope.
The separately mapped railway station stays independent. Grading is approximate based on the public composite terrain field.
